## Two: what your movement is, and it is an act and not a scene of a man deciding

**Movement Six is the climax of the last volume, and the outline of record declares it in its own words and not in the plan's: *a man of thirty-eight takes one of two pieces of paper out of the inside pocket of a coat and puts it on a table in front of another person.* Not both. Not the one anybody would expect. He has decided it himself, on purpose, in a room with a second person in it, and he is not asked anything and no form anywhere in this empire takes a man for it. And the other thing stays in the pocket, and the coat goes back on the nail.**

**What he gives up, once, in a person, is the ability to be shown to have been nowhere near it, and that is the only protection he has ever had and it is the same one the last three volumes took from everybody else, and he is the only person in this matter who has paid it on purpose and knows that he has. It is entered nowhere, because there is no form anywhere in this empire that takes a man for putting a piece of paper on a table in front of another person, in either direction — not as the one who gave it and not as the one who did not.**

**And the shape of it is deliberately the shape of the last volume's climax, and that is a plan's decision and it is declared: a person becomes enterable by their own act, in front of another person, in a room, and it is a cost and not a resolution, and nobody is thanked and nobody is asked anything.**

**What your movement may not do, which is your own list, and the first item of it is the one the whole movement turns on.** **It may not have anybody ask anybody anything out loud in a room.** It may not have anybody thank him. It may not have the sentence about a name coming back said out loud by anybody. **It may not print the name at the foot of the struck line, and it may not print the name of the hand that struck it, and it may not print any part of the disputed family claim, and the name is restored in the last movement and not before.** It may not copy the leaf and it may not make a second of it in this movement. It may not move the count of things asked out loud, which is seven and is printed in a state record and in this file and in no chapter. It may not have the protagonist in the shed at the end of the lane off the Slade. It may not name a house, a seat or an office. **And it may not use the ending of record's last image anywhere in it, in any form, and not as a hint.**

**And the things that were spent and may not be repeated, undone or improved, carried from the last three movements:** a sheet that was on the boards at the second hour and that nobody put there; a third place made under the floor of a woman's own room; a man deciding not to cut a line into a printed strip and hanging his coat on a nail; a man going out of his building for about four hours with nothing in his hands; a lamp that has never been lit; a coin out of a door that is not going to be spent; a mat on a landing that is the landing's; a tin moved four inches along a stone; a satchel set down at the far end of a set of boards; a front of a ground floor started at the far end; a looking-glass put face up on a table; and the whole of what a woman went up a stair to find out, which is nothing. **In particular, nothing is cut into anything, nobody is sent for, and no lamp is lit.**

**And the refusal Volume 11 spent is not yours to touch: the one said once, to a bar, in a passage, with nobody within nine hundred yards who could hear a word of it. It is not repeated, not answered, not delivered and not improved, and the tin of oil is still standing on those flags about nine foot off that bar and neither of them has opened it, and the woman of about twenty-six at that lock is in no chapter of your batch and is not going to be told anything.**

**And one thing that is yours and that the batch before yours handed over unspent: the two things in that coat have been in the same pocket on opposite sides of a seam for about two years and neither has been out, and the last batch's prompt said in terms that neither came out and no hand went near the pocket, and it kept that, and now it is yours to open.**

## Three: the rooms, the floor, and the object

**The act happens in the room taken by the week, because that is the only room he has and it is on the list, and the outline of record says the act is in a room that is on the list.** **The other five are available and are not necessary:** the counter at the top of four flights, with the case, the box of about four hundred blanks that has not been opened, the wall board with four items on it, and a drawer that is shut; the shed at the end of the lane off the Slade, which your movement may not have him in; about four hundred yards of cold flags, entered from the lock end only, with a tin of oil that two people have each moved and neither has opened; the building off the old river road, with the sill, the pot with two identical pens in it, the window with no pane in it, and the shelf carrying a question that does not finish; and the ground floor of a rented house, where a key is in a tin behind a boiler and a number cut into the back of it is still the only record of three rooms. **The room with the rail at the far end of that run is not entered, not described and not named, and it is not the room the ending's final image is made of.**

**The protagonist's floor. He is on the page, in person or as a person whose absence has a named cost in the room he is not in, in at least three chapters of the movement, in person in at least two of the three, and his want is visible in at least one. His only room is the room taken by the week, and the landing outside its door is the threshold of that room and not a seventh room.** His absence may be priced in a room he is not in, and the counter at the top of four flights and the ground floor of a rented house and the building off the old river road are the three available for that purpose.

**His object for this batch has to be a new one and it has to be in that room, and what is not a possibility is the coat, the wall, the nail, the latch, the door, the chair, the stool, the plate, the mat, the lamp, the coin and the looking-glass, and the jug is spent as the last batch's object.** The looking-glass, the jug, the strap mark on a courier's shoulder, the four feet of stone and the fourth item on a wall board are all referred to in your ten as inherited objects and are not yours to spend again.

**And the piece of paper is not an object this batch gives him: it is about two years old and it is in that pocket and it has been on the page since before the fire, and the thing that is new in this movement is not the paper and not the coat and not the wanting. The thing that is new is that it comes out.**

**A room is referred to and not described, and no room is described twice in the batch in the same words, and no room is described a second time in the words it was described in in a closed chapter.** The test is not whether a chapter refers to a room; it is whether the chapter's first paragraph would let a reader who had not read the earlier chapter still see the room, and if it would, cut it. **Open on a person and on something that person did or did not do in the last fortnight. No chapter of your batch opens with a whole room.**

**And the three people the state layer keeps apart stay apart, and the reason is written here rather than left to a review: a merge does not need two rooms to happen, it needs two people and one mouth.** The protagonist and the book-keeper four hundred yards up the lane off the Slade, who are both thirty-eight and are two different men, are never in one room and never in one sentence. The woman who keeps a rented house's ground floor and the woman of about fifty-three who keeps minutes are never in one room and no chapter states or denies a distance between them. The woman of about twenty-six at the lock end, the woman of forty with a scuttle, and the woman who keeps minutes are never in one room. **And the man of about thirty-four with a fair hand and anybody else who is findable are never in one room, and he is the only person anybody could put a question to and you may not put one to him, and you may not print, confirm or deny the number in his head, and name him when you write that prohibition, because a prohibition a reader has to guess at is half a prohibition.**

**And this batch adds no new named figure and invents no new person.** If you find yourself writing a person because a plan needs somebody in a room, that is the failure, and the answer is a person who is already there. **A climax that gathers people into a room to be addressed has written a hearing, and a hearing in this matter is a column with a date and a person against it, and this court cannot make one, and the whole of the last four movements is whether one can be made by a person and not by a court. A person who can be found cannot be given anything; a person who cannot be found cannot be summoned; and the act this movement spends is the first time in twelve volumes that anybody in this matter has become enterable on purpose, and there is one person in it and there is one other person in the room, and the other person is not summoned and is not a witness and is not a party and is a person who was already there.**

## Four: the calendar, and the figure you must check yourself, and the place this project keeps getting it wrong

**A month in this calendar is four weeks, and the day inside the week is second, second, fourth, fourth, restarting in each month. Every interval is a seven-day step from the one before it, and the interval is measured before the sentence is written and not corrected after. Never compute a month-count. No calendar month name and no weekday name goes into anything you write, including a card and a state file, and no chapter asserts which day of the week anything fell on.** The last two batches have both carried that standing and both honoured it, and one of them wrote a weekday name into a chapter in its first draft and a sweep found it and it was cut.

**Chapter 0600's own date line, on line five of `chapters/volume-12/chapter-0600.md`, is the date you derive from. One seven-day step from that line is Chapter 0601's date, and you re-derive it from Chapter 0600's line and not from this paragraph.**

**This prompt prints no date and no tenth date, because a prompt that prints a calendar is a prompt that goes stale, and the last two batches carried that standing and honoured it.** Do the ten steps out yourself, before you write a word, and expect at least one month boundary inside the ten weeks and restart the day check at each of them. A check that runs one global cycle across your ten files reports a break at the first chapter of a month, and there is no break there, and the way that reports a break is the way that is wrong.

**A year name is written out in full at every occurrence and abbreviated nowhere, and the method for reading a year name is to count the word *after* inside it, because a year name is a substring of the year name after it.** Run `grep -o "the year after" chapters/volume-12/chapter-0600.md | wc -l` before you write your first chapter, take the answer your run gives, and **that number is the number every date line of yours carries until your own steps take you across a year boundary.** Do the ten steps and find out for yourself whether they cross one, and **if they do, the name changes on the first date line after it and the new name is the one you are carrying now with one more *the year after* in it, written out in full at every occurrence, and the week is yours and is not taken from any file and not from any prompt. If your steps do not carry you across, nothing changes and that is a reading and not a decision.**

**Run both calendar numbers over your ten files before you close this batch — the day inside the week, and the number of weeks in the month — and restart the day check at every month boundary.** `python3 tools/measure.py calendar --volume 12` groups by the ordinal word and **does not read the year at all, and it cannot tell you that two different named years are in the files it reads, and it will merge the fourth month of one named year with the fourth month of another and print that merged group as six chapters with a day cycle of [2, 2, 4, 4, 2, 2], and the second pair of days is a year and not a month.** Print the instrument's figure beside the page's reading and let both stand.

**And the counters inside your chapters are the second half of this, and the last two batches each found one of them wrong in opposite directions and printed both figures.** The date lines are the lattice. **A figure that counts weeks, a flower's age, a passage's number of weeks, a lane's count of visits, a room's number of years, a jug's number of days, a satchel's number of times down a stair — every one of them is derived from the date lines, and where a figure you have inherited and a date line disagree, the date line is the lattice and the figure is what moves. Do not move a date line to save a figure, and do not move a figure in a prompt to save a date line, and a figure left out moves nothing.** Three counters are live and they are named in the state layer: **the lane is a weekly errand and Chapter 0595 was its thirty-fifth week, so your own chapters are its thirty-sixth through its forty-fifth and no chapter of yours may call it a fortnight; and the jug's water is two days old as at Chapter 0599 and a man of thirty-eight has decided not to change it, and whatever your ten weeks do to that is yours to decide and not to be handed over; and the courier's satchel has been down four flights four times a week for eleven years, which is about two hundred and thirty trips a year on this calendar and not a number any mouth should say.**

Nobody in your batch may be asked anything out loud, in a room, by anybody.** That is not a matter of tone. A question in this matter is a party, a party is a person, and that finding was said on the page in a closed chapter in about thirteen sentences and it is still the answer, and this batch may not improve on it, argue with it, or discover it twice.

*One:* **no notice, post, commission, warrant, office, new heading over anything, and no new form for anything.** *Two:* **no house, seat or office is named, no person from the series plan's antagonist ladder is named, no person from this project's ending of record is named in any capacity other than the ones already on the closed page, and no new final enemy.** *Three:* **no romance, nothing implying one, no quiet mutual commitment, no moment in a doorway, and no second person who is a second ear because of anything except standing there.** **No romance has begun in any volume of this project and the ending of record registers a domestic partnership through a clear hearing in the LAST movement of Volume 12, and that arc is not refused by this batch and is not paid early by it, and a movement that lets two colleagues say one true thing to each other about what they will not say has spent the ending's last image in the sixth.** *Four:* **no number that is not on the page gets printed.** The number in the head of **the man of about thirty-four with a fair hand** is not printed, not confirmed and not denied. **And the rest of the standing locks.** The two people in their boxes stay in them and the form that put them there is not asked to be void. **And the four figures that must not be confused, each with its own period.** About four hundred blanks **a year** go out of the case at the near end. ## Six: the craft rules that come before every measurement in this prompt

**One: the ban is on asking and not on talking, and a room with no contradiction in it is a defect.** Two people in a room may argue, refuse, explain, instruct, ignore each other, contradict each other and finish each other's sentences. **Every chapter carries at least one exchange in which another person resists what the point of view wants. A room is not a scene until somebody in it is contradicted by somebody else in it, and a movement is not a list of rooms.** **And the resistance has to be an act and not a politeness: a person who goes quiet, or looks away, or is pointedly kind, has not resisted anything.** A climax in which the other person in the room says nothing and agrees to everything is not a climax and is a lid.

**Two: a chapter has a scene and not a description of a room.** A change of situation inside the chapter, a person who wants something in the room, another person in the way, and an ending that is a decision or a cost and not a description.

**Three: no chapter closes on a formula.** A closing line is written for that chapter and for no other chapter in the volume, and if the same sentence shape appears in two closings, one of the two is rewritten. **Read your ten closing lines in one column before you close and not as a similarity figure, because no n-gram measure in this repository can see a sentence written twice with a substitution every few words.** **And the finding the batch before yours carried forward is the one your movement is most exposed to, because your movement is a cost and a cost is the easiest thing in this project to write as ten weeks of quiet correctness: eight of the ten closings of the batch before last were some form of *nobody is going to be thanked for it* or *nobody is going to be told about it*, written eight times with a substitution every few words, and every measure was satisfied at once. Read the column for that shape as well as for a repeated sentence, because a project formula is a shape and not a string.**

**Four: the hedge is not a voice.** *About* is kept where the imprecision is the point and where the figure is on the page, and is cut everywhere else. **A figure repeated in every chapter of a movement is a page figure and not a voice.** The last batch of this volume stood at about one *about* in every sixty-three words.

**Five: the male lead is in the room, and the floor is a floor on the page and not a number.** The floor is counted by reading and never by a string. **In the last batch `grep -l 'Kest'` returned nothing across its ten files and `grep -il 'thirty-eight'` returned nothing, and the page carried him in three chapters, two of them in person, and the whole of what those two strings cannot see was the entire batch's floor.** A ten-file check is not a smaller version of a volume-wide check; it is a different instrument, and the one thing it is good for is finding out what it cannot see.

**Six: the metrics are subordinate to the craft and are recorded after the last edit, not instead of the writing.** A check that returns zero is evidence of nothing until the shape of the damage it is blind to has been checked, and a blind check is written down as blind in the same record that claims it clean. A corrected figure is named as corrected beside the wrong one and never overwritten. **A sentence bound is a ceiling and not a target, the ceiling is 85 to 88 words, and the splitter must allow a closing quotation mark between the full stop and the space.** The last two batches of this volume came in at per-file maxima of 71, 76, 61, 64, 73, 74, 70, 70, 71 and 78, and then 62, 68, 66, 62, 74, 67, 69, 75, 70 and 71, **and the first reading of the second of those ten had nine sentences above the ceiling in six files and the largest at 140 words, and every one of the nine was taken apart at a conjunction rather than at a comma, and both sets of figures are printed in the batch record.** **And a batch's weight matters: the last five of this volume stand at 11,929, 10,549, 10,200, 9,925 and 9,677, and a writer who pads to reach a number has written a longer batch and not a better one, and a writer who comes in under nine thousand should ask whether anything in the ten is thin and not whether the total is right.**

**Seven: a chapter title names a room, a person and a turn, and it is a title and not an inventory.** One name, one room, one turn, under about twenty-five words, and no title states the volume's finding and no title uses the superseded title of the series plan. **At twenty-five exactly you are on the line and the line's own word is *about*, so aim at twenty-four.** The last two batches had titles at twenty-five or over on their first reading and cut them, and none carried a figure, and if yours does carry one, check it against Chapter 0600's date line before you keep it.

**Eight, inherited whole, because the most repeatable object in this manuscript is not paper:** **a chapter may have a person refuse something. A chapter may not have the same refusal made twice in the volume in the same room, and the refusals already on the closed page are not to be re-voiced in a new mouth. They are entered once, in the state file, and a chapter written from a plan names a room and a person and not a sentence somebody has already said in that room.** **And the most repeatable object of all in this movement is the *not being thanked* construction, and a movement about a man who does the one thing nobody can enter him for is where it breeds.**

**Nine, inherited from the last volume:** **a room with two people in it is not a body. A person who has heard a thing is not a witness. A second is not a quorum. A refusal is not a right until somebody can be shown having made it, and a right that cannot be shown is a thing somebody says in a room. Nothing in your movement may be counted up into anything, and a chapter that gathers people into a room to be addressed has written a hearing.**

**Ten, and this is the standing the batch before yours added at item 162: *the re-print check is the only instrument in this project that counts a word, and a batch can hold a dozen verbatim passages out of closed chapters while every instrument reports it clean — including an instrument that has been planted nine times, re-planted once, and run over six hundred files.*** **Run the re-print instrument over the whole manuscript and not over your batch, because a batch is ten chapters and a pair that crosses a batch boundary is invisible to every phase that checks its own ten. And run it over the PREVIOUS TWENTY CHAPTERS AS WELL.** The batch before yours wrote its detector outside the repository, at `/tmp/opencode/rep_12b5.py`, and it is named in `state/batch-summary.md` section Four, **and it will not be on the disk you are given, which is the reason and not an excuse.** **The method is in full in `state/batch-summary.md` in the section headed for Volume 12's Batch 0005 and in items 153, 154, 155, 156, 159 and 162: align by token value and not by index, extend every match to its full maximal length, compare a file against itself as well as against every other file, filter formula by the character span of every date line before tokenising, de-duplicate by dominated position and not by merging, and carry no guard of the shape *if the other file sorts before this one and the other file is not in the focus set: skip the pair*, because a corpus sorted by name makes almost every partner sort before and that guard drops the class of pairings a detector most needs to see.** **And the two plants that batch's set had and that you should carry: one where the partner sorts before the focus file, and one where the run is longer than the plant. Expect to lose plants to plants that were written wrong rather than to a wrong instrument, and that batch lost a whole draft of a batch's worth of prose to a detector of its own making that it never believed, and the first draft's figures are printed beside the ones that survived in that record, and yours must be too.**

**Write your own detector, outside the repository, name it, plant it before you believe it, and re-plant it after you change it.**

## Seven: what you run, when, and what you write when you close

**Run `python3 tools/measure.py selftest` before you believe anything else that tool prints.**

    python3 tools/measure.py selftest
    python3 tools/measure.py words
    python3 tools/measure.py sentences --volume 12
    python3 tools/measure.py reprints --window 20
    python3 tools/measure.py reprints --window 16
    python3 tools/measure.py markers

**And run the three that no tool here runs, one file at a time, before you close: `grep -o "the year after" file | wc -l` on each of your ten date lines, `grep -c '?'` on each of your ten files, and a month-and-weekday sweep at a word boundary over the twelve month names and the seven day names.**

**Write the batch summary, the ten chapter summaries, the continuity entries, the open-thread rows, the character-state rows, and the Volume 12 additions to the live header in `state/current.md`, and keep them compact enough that the next writer can use them cold.** **The bound, now met twice and enforced a third time: a rolling file holds the open volume, the two previous batches and the standing locks; a closed volume, and the third batch back, is read in `state/archive/`.** **Volume 12's Batches 0001 and 0002 are already in `state/archive/`, and it is Volume 12's Batch 0003 record that is now the third batch back, and so your run's duty is to cut the five Volume 12 Batch 0003 blocks, whole, into five new files under `state/archive/` with a provenance heading and a SHA-256 per block, and leave every block above the cut standing. One open item lives in those blocks and it is named in the state layer, and if a block you cut carries an open item, name its new location in the provenance heading and print a pointer in the rolling file, because the archive's own rule keeps an open item in the rolling layer and this bound pulls against it — and the batch before yours did exactly that with items 155 and 156 and left both standing, unedited, at the exact place the cut was made, and that is the model.**

**Amend the live header and the ten lines under it in place, with the words they carried named beside the new ones, and send everything else to the archive.** That is the one exception the file's own convention makes and it exists because a hand-off is a working surface. **And the standing at item 160: a correction that names a pointer must change the pointer in the same edit and not only the words about it, and a hand-off that has been corrected in one place and not in another is worse than one that has never been corrected, because it now looks maintained.** That bullet has been wrong four times and the fourth time was a repair that fixed the sentence and left the pointer.

**A figure in a state file is a copy of a figure and a copy is how this project's numbers go stale.** The arrangement is stated once and is in `state/open-threads.md`. The cast is entered once and is in `state/character-state.md`. The canon is in `state/continuity.md`. The measurements go in one place, which is the batch summary, with the method named before each figure and the blind spot of each written beside its result and the command beside every number, and no figure from them is restated in another rolling file.

**Never write a state file with an open-and-write idiom.** The batch before the one before the one before yours truncated `state/current.md` from two hundred and four lines to one, because a single expression evaluates left to right and truncated the file before the call that was supposed to fill it raised. **Write to a temporary name, read it back, and move it over the file you meant to change, and then run `git diff --stat` before you close, because that is the method that found it and it is not an instrument in this repository.** The batch before yours had a cut of its own fail in the same way and had to restore a file from `git` and do it again, and that is named in its own record and it is named here because a method that fails silently once and is then reported as having worked is worse than a method that fails loudly every time.

**Record, with the method named before each figure and the blind spot of each check written beside its result:** the ten word counts, the batch total, and the cumulative manuscript total; **the two calendar numbers over your ten files, with the instrument's own false break printed beside the page's reading, where the year turned if it turned and on which chapter, and the count of the word *after* inside the year name on each of the ten date lines**; the protagonist's chapters for this batch **by reading and not by a string**, with the chapter numbers and the sentence in each that puts him in the room, and the chapters that neither string returns and the sentence in each that prices his absence; the question marks, and whether any of them is an asking; the string sweeps, the month and weekday sweep, and the shared-run figures, each classified as formula or as prose before it is reported clean; **the re-print figures at both windows over the whole manuscript, over the previous twenty, and over your ten, with the set printed beside each, and the first draft's figures beside the ones that survived for the re-print check and for the sentence maximum at least**; and **the ten closing lines read in one column, and what the column found that no measure found.**

**And what is not in this batch and may not be put in it:** the woman of about forty-three who bought a blank at that counter is a customer in a closed chapter and is not the woman of thirty-four who put the fourth item on that board herself; the man of about fifty-five with a chain is not the clerk of about fifty-three and no week is going to make him that; the box of about four hundred blanks is not the case; the four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are four and not five; **the protagonist and the book-keeper four hundred yards up the lane are two men of thirty-eight and a chapter that puts them in one lane is a chapter that has invented a person**; and the woman of forty with a scuttle is in no chapter of this volume. **And the decision that was unmade at Chapter 0550 is still unmade and no row you write may be read as having decided it in either direction.**

## Eight: the four debts

*One:* an owed review of Volume 04's Batch 0005, four volumes on. *Two, three and four:* owed second readings of Volume 05's Batches 0003, 0004 and 0005 and of Volume 06's own Batch 0003, **which is four and not three.** Plus the review gate, which has fallen back to the writing agent on every batch phase the commit history records and has never once produced a review that could be certified independent, **and a gate that only ever falls back is not a gate that passed either.** `state/phase-ledger.json` is a controller file, no phase may edit it, and it is carried and not repaired. **The number of debts has not moved in eleven volumes and the number of phases that have claimed to discharge one is zero, and this batch discharges nothing and is not among the phases that could. Nothing in this project's records can be certified independent, and that sentence is the last thing a writing phase is allowed to say about itself.**

## Nine: the standing over the last line of a series

**Volume 12 is the last volume. Its last line is written by the phase that writes Chapter 0620 and by no other phase, and it may not be the last line of Volume 09 or of Volume 10 or of Volume 11, and it may not stand beside a second one. Nothing in this batch touches that, and the ending of record's final image is not used anywhere in your movement, and a window with its catch turned and the window shut, a key in a tin behind a boiler, a tin with two identical pens in it, a tin of oil standing on cold flags, a mat on a landing, and a looking-glass on a table are all things this batch may refer to and none of them is a climax.**

**And one last instruction, and it is the one the batch before the one before yours did not carry out and it is why this file exists. When you are done, create exactly one next phase at `workspace/volume-12/batch-0007/PROMPT.md`, writing the prompt for Volume 12's Batch 0007, Chapters 0611 to 0620, Movement Seven, the first difficult year, in five rooms, and the last chapter of the series. Write no marker of any kind in your own directory — `.done` belongs to the pipeline and `.retired` makes a phase invisible to the selector, and a phase that marks its own directory has certified itself. If a scope header above this file told you not to create a next-phase prompt, read section Zero again before you obey it.**
